citation.authors: So LL, Davis PJ, King NM
citation.title: Wits appraisal in southern Chinese children

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08: norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 4 differences (logs/task9a2-compare-<id>.log). Every mean and SD of both extractors re-read from the page images (PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24), and the settled file checked by script against a third, independent reading of the pages (the table in sets.test.ts). Decisions: (0) Source text normalised to one pattern giving table, page, row and column with sex and age (a and b worded it differently; prose only). (1) n 55 and 46: b only, from the text p. 22 ('55 males and 46 females') -> kept. Page images: PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24 (Tables I-VI), rendered at 2000 px.

caveats: Quoted second-hand from Moate & Darendeliler 2002 (Aust Orthod J 18:19-26, a compilation of published Chinese cephalometric norms), Table V; the original paper was not read. The compilation rounds every mean and SD to whole numbers (Lew's soft tissue to 0.5) and gives no landmark, plane or method definitions.
The compilation states no film scale or magnification for any study; assumed true size (owner ruling M-2).
101 southern Chinese children aged 10 to 15 (55 males, 46 females), randomly selected from 1,605 cephalometric films on file in Hong Kong (text p. 22).
Table V prints the Wits values in its '18 Years +' columns, but So's sample was 10 to 15 years old: entered at 10-15 (merge notes).

Wits to the functional occlusal plane (text pp. 22 and 25), with Jacobson's sign (Jacobson: -1 mm Caucasian males, 0 females, p. 22): same as catalogue #13. No SD printed; the app borrows one where a matching paper has it (Task 4c).
The other rows of Table V average several studies and are not entered.
The text (p. 22) passes on So's warning that nasion is hard to locate in southern Chinese films (the shallow nasal bridge overlaps the eyelids' tarsal plates).
